issues: Emergent visual-editor injects <span data-ve-dynamic='true'> inside <option> elements → 4 identical hydration warnings emitted per page. Not application code. Already documented in iterations 34–36. No functional impact.

critical_code_review_comments: FIXED in this iteration: trust_authenticity.audit_log() used `async for` over `db.<collection>.find(...).to_list(200)` which returns a Future (motor coroutine), not an async iterator. Result: /api/trust/audit/{product_id} returned 500 for every call. Changed to `for l in await db.<collection>.find(...).to_list(200):`. This was the ONLY functional defect found in the new Trust+QICS surface — verified fixed by re-running test_audit_returns_events_list which now passes.

trust_authenticity.py L157: `verify_url = f"{verify_base_url}/api/trust/verify/{code}" if verify_base_url else f"/api/trust/verify/{code}"` — when a request comes from behind the K8s ingress the base_url is `https://<preview>.emergentagent.com/`, so the QR encodes a URL that points to the same origin. Good. However `authenticity_certificate()` is also called from `qics.activate()` where the QR is instead built from `portal_url`, and BOTH are stored on the same record — consider making the QR/verify_url derivation explicit rather than incidental.

trust_authenticity.py PROTECTION_LAYERS: three layers report status='enforced' but PLATFORM_CAPABILITIES marks etsy.supported=[] and podcast_platforms.supported=[]. Watermarking is applied everywhere as an 'always' baseline (line 207), yet a customer publishing to Etsy technically only gets metadata+watermark baked in by QRU-native rendering (not enforced by Etsy). Copy is honest ('Enforced Now' + 'best_available' note), but consider surfacing a per-platform-per-layer effective status in the Trust page so a Founder can see 'Watermarking = Enforced (rendering-side) · Not Enforceable Post-Sale (Etsy allows PDF download)'.

qics.py assign_identity() uses find_one_and_update({prefix}, {$inc:{seq:1}}, upsert=True, return_document=True). If two activate calls race for the SAME product but its qics_identity is still None, both will pass the `if p.get('qics_identity')` guard, both will $inc the counter, and both will $set a different identity on the product (last write wins). The QICS 'immutable identity' promise is only true under single-writer semantics. Recommend: use `find_one_and_update({id, qics_identity: None}, {$set:{qics_identity:<computed_after_$inc>}})` and check `updated_existing` OR return the pre-existing identity, so two racing calls always return the same value.

routers/qics.py activate() persists `portal` (full 15-section snapshot) into `qics_portals` on every activation, but portal() also rebuilds sections live from `companion_portal(db, p)`. The stored portal is therefore stale on the next scan and only used as a fallback when the product doc is missing. Either drop the stored portal (rely on live rebuild) or store it as a `last_snapshot` for archive/audit clarity — mixing both roles causes confusion.

TrustRegistry.js loadCert(): silently swallows errors with `catch { toast.error(...) }` — no error is stored to state, so if a Founder dismisses the toast they will see a blank cert area with no explanation. Consider setting an inline error message inside `trust-cert-panel`.

TrustRegistry.js and CompanionSystem.js both re-use `/api/founder-inbox` as their product catalog source (same anti-pattern flagged in iterations 35/36 for VisualStudio + MediaStarterKit). A dedicated `/api/products` catalog endpoint would decouple these pages from the Founder-inbox operational feed and make them usable by non-Founder super-admins in the future.

CompanionSystem.js loadPortals() re-fetches only after activate(), but on activation failure `finally { setBusy(false) }` runs — the toast fires but there is no inline error state on qics-activator. Consider surfacing the failure inside the panel.

Bug fixed this iteration: trust_authenticity.audit_log() had `async for l in <coroutine>` — the .to_list(200) result is a coroutine, so it must be `for l in await <coroutine>`. All 20 pytest cases pass in ~3.6s (single-worker; parallel xdist can be re-enabled by removing `-p no:xdist -o addopts=""`).
rca of the issue: ONE defect found and fixed in this iteration: /api/trust/audit/{product_id} returned 500. Reproduction: GET /api/trust/audit/<any-product-id> with a valid Founder bearer token → 500. Backend log showed `TypeError: 'async for' requires an object with __aiter__ method, got _asyncio.Future` at trust_authenticity.py:224. Root cause: `.to_list(200)` on a motor cursor already resolves the cursor to a Python list (as a coroutine that must be `await`ed); iterating with `async for` on the coroutine object is invalid. Mitigation: replaced all three `async for l in db.<c>.find(...).to_list(200)` with `for l in await db.<c>.find(...).to_list(200)` in audit_log() (lines 224/227/230). Verified fixed — TestTrustPlatformPlan.test_audit_returns_events_list now passes and manual call returns {product_code, events:[], total:0}. No other defects observed in Trust+QICS surface. Prior fix (rendering design_gate dict as a React child in _approval_history() / gold_status()) is holding — cert loaded on /trust for PRD-00078 rendered 2 approval rows with proper string decisions and no ErrorBoundary.
